{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Cake|Cake]]

A traditional '''pound cake''' recipe would specify one pound each of flour, butter, eggs, and sugar. These quantities are too great for most modern families, but an excellent cake can be made with half quantities. It is usual to weigh the eggs first and then use the same weights of the other ingredients; with a traditional pair of kitchen scales, the eggs are simply used instead of weights.

== Ingredients ==
*½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] self-raising [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*½ pound [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*½ pound (4 [[Cookbook:Each|ea.]]) [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
*½ pound [[Cookbook:Superfine Sugar|caster sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] extract (optional)
*½ pound assorted dried fruit ([[Cookbook:Currant|currants]], [[Cookbook:Sultana|sultanas]], and [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]], with perhaps a lesser quantity of [[Cookbook:Maraschino Cherry|glacé cherries]]; optional)

== Procedure ==
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|175°C (350°F or Gas Mark 4)]].
#[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] the butter and sugar together until fluffy.
#[[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] in the eggs and add the vanilla extract.
#Gradually [[Cookbook:Sifting|sift]] in the dry ingredients.
#Transfer to a greased and floured [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]].
#[[Cookbook:Bake|Bake]] for 35 minutes or until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] inserted shows no moist crumbs when removed.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] (or lb) is equal to 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] or 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] or approximately 227 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]] (or g). Needless to say, in this recipe, 250 grams of each ingredient could be used.
